object.description: The Wright Flyer is the biplane in which Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first sustained, controlled flights of a powered, heavier-than-air aircraft at Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, on 17 December 1903. Built in the brothers' Dayton bicycle shop, it combined a wing-warping control system with a purpose-built 12-horsepower petrol engine and twin pusher propellers. This is the Smithsonian's laser scan of the original aircraft as it hangs in the National Air and Space Museum.
facts: Four flights were made on 17 December 1903; the longest covered 852 ft (260 m) in 59 seconds.
The 12-horsepower engine was built from scratch in six weeks by the Wrights' mechanic Charlie Taylor, with a cast-aluminium crankcase.
The Flyer joined the Smithsonian collection in 1948 after a long dispute between Orville Wright and the Institution over who flew first.

tour: The 1903 Wright Flyer, the machine itself. Twelve seconds in the air at Kitty Hawk, the first powered flight with a person aboard.
